assigned.title: Production composition registers the catalog ingestion runtime
assigned.acceptance: A hosted deployment that is configured for a real catalog source actually gets one: something in the production composition root calls registerCatalogIngestionRuntime with a runtime built next to the Node pinned-fetch construction. PL-0305 made the application CAPABLE of hosting the real source and the reviewer accepted that as complete; what remains is that NOTHING CALLS THE REGISTRATION, so a hosted deployment still answers no_metadata_source_configured -- a true statement about the deployment rather than about the registry, and the exact gap this task owns. Required: the runtime is built from the existing pinned-fetch transport rather than a second fetch path; NO CREDENTIAL OR API KEY IS INTRODUCED, since the initial source needs none and an ambient key would be the hidden credentialed source PL-0305's review forbade; an unconfigured deployment must STILL refuse by name rather than silently acquiring a default; and a regression must drive the composition root and observe a configured resolution, because a registration nobody has watched fire is not known to work. OUT OF SCOPE: persistent scheduling and storage, which is PL-0309, and the rights register, which is not a coding task. NOTE BEFORE CLAIMING: the exact composition-root file may not exist yet; the declared surface names the likely homes and must be corrected before the claim rather than widened after, on the PL-0710 precedent.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 0 cached, 2642 passed 1 skipped (2617 before this wave). server-bootstrap.test.ts 16 passed; apps/web src/lib plus the entry point 162 passed. THE ENTRY POINT WAS PROVED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT CORRECTED THIS LEAD. My pre-claim surface correction moved instrumentation.ts to apps/web/ on the belief Next reads it from the app root; the implementer replayed Next 16.3.1's own findPagesDir and getFilesInDir and showed rootDir = path.join(pagesDir || appDir, '..') resolves to apps/web/src for a src/app project, so a file at the app root is NEVER LOADED -- and it REFUSED TO WRITE THE FILE AT MY DECLARED PATH rather than produce something Next never loads sitting where the wiring appears to be. The surface was corrected on that evidence and the probe now resolves instrumentationHookFilePath to /src/instrumentation.ts against the real tree, with a root-placed fixture resolving nothing as the control. VALUE-RED on the entry point: flipping the runtime guard from nodejs to node gives 2 failed 14 passed, 'runs the bootstrap in the Node runtime and the registry then resolves configured' and 'says so at startup when nothing is configured'. The ORIGINAL red for the composition root could only be module-resolution -- 'Cannot find module ./server-bootstrap', no tests collected -- because the gap this task owns is the ABSENCE OF A CALLER: there was no root to hand a wrong value, and the behaviour a value-red would assert already passed. Stated rather than smoothed. THE CREDENTIAL ASSERTION EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY: it is checked in two halves, every declared name against /KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|CRED|AUTH/i and the module's own source text against the declared set so a second undeclared read cannot hide, and it failed on the first green run because a comment named LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET -- 'expected [LIBERTY_BUILD_TARGET, ...(8)] to deeply equal [...(7)]'. The pinned transport is asserted by REFERENCE IDENTITY, expect(runtime.provider.transport.fetchImpl).toBe(nodePinnedFetch), because a second fetch path that happened to work would satisfy any behavioural check. rightsRegister is noRightsBasisEstablished by reference, so a configured deployment publishes nothing and says per record why.

assigned.surfaceCorrectedTwiceBeforeCompletion: SECOND CORRECTION 2026-09-20, mid-implementation, AND IT REVERSES THE FIRST ONE. My pre-claim correction moved instrumentation.ts from apps/web/src/ to apps/web/ on the belief that Next reads it from the app root. THAT WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER PROVED IT rather than asserting it: Next 16.3.1 discovers the file in exactly one directory, non-recursively, at rootDir = path.join(pagesDir || appDir, '..'), so for an app with src/app and no pages/ the directory is apps/web/src and a file at apps/web/instrumentation.ts is NEVER LOADED. It replayed Next's own findPagesDir and getFilesInDir over this tree and over two throwaway fixtures differing only in the file's location, and the fixture with the file at the app root produced no instrumentationHookFilePath at all. It then REFUSED TO WRITE THE FILE AT THE DECLARED PATH, on the ground that a file Next never loads, sitting where the wiring appears to be, is worse than no file. That is the right call and the surface is corrected to match the evidence, which is exactly the bar the human commander set this round for touching a removed path. REMOVED as proved unnecessary: apps/web/instrumentation.ts (the wrong path); apps/web/next.config.ts (Next 16.3.1 needs no opt-in -- next/dist/server/config.js deprecates experimental.instrumentationHook with 'instrumentation.js is available by default', so the file earned no edit); docs/DEPLOYMENT.md (the operator note is a fact about this source and belongs in docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md, which already carries the licensing decision and the rights position, and the repo has no other deployment-runbook content for a new file to sit beside). assigned.title: One authoritative provider health floor, consumed by both packages
assigned.acceptance: ONE authoritative provider-health-floor vocabulary exists and BOTH @liberty/provider-sdk and @liberty/media-engine consume it, with no second literal of the value anywhere in production code. THE DUPLICATION, stated exactly. packages/media-engine/src/ranking.ts:83 declares `export const PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR = 0.5` and line 128 compares `candidate.healthScore < PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR` to produce the `provider_health_below_floor` reason. packages/provider-sdk/src/health.ts:216 separately sets `failBelow: 0.5` in its default policy and line 604 compares `score < policy.failBelow` to produce the `fail` verdict. Three comments in health.ts (lines 177, 391 and 405) and one runtime message (line 625) already ASSERT that the two agree. An assertion in prose is exactly what does not survive an edit to one of the two numbers, which is the whole finding. REQUIRED: the shared declaration lands in a package both consumers ALREADY depend on, or in a new dependency-leaf package, and the implementer states which and why. Measured 2026-09-21: @liberty/media-engine depends on @liberty/contracts only; @liberty/provider-sdk depends on @liberty/contracts, @liberty/media-inspection, @liberty/net-policy and zod; @liberty/contracts depends on zod only. So @liberty/contracts is today the only existing package that both consume and that cannot import either of them, and putting the floor there adds no edge at all. A new leaf on the @liberty/net-policy pattern is also acceptable if the implementer can show why contracts is the wrong home. Adding an edge from media-engine to provider-sdk is NOT acceptable: provider-sdk is the provider-adapter isolation boundary (invariant 3) and media-engine is downstream of it. REQUIRED: a check that FAILS if the two ever disagree again, and it must not be satisfiable by a comment. Either the two consumers read the same exported symbol -- so disagreement is unrepresentable rather than merely tested -- or, where a policy field must stay independently configurable, a test asserts the default policy's `failBelow` equals the authoritative floor and would go red on either number alone being changed. If both mechanisms are used, say which one carries the guarantee. REQUIRED: the two comparisons keep their CURRENT and DIFFERENT boundary semantics, or the change of semantics is deliberate and stated. media-engine excludes a candidate strictly BELOW the floor; provider-sdk returns `fail` strictly BELOW `failBelow`. These agree today. A refactor that quietly moves either to `<=` changes which providers serve, and sharing one constant must not be allowed to smuggle that in. PRESERVED INVARIANT, non-negotiable: health may only SUBTRACT eligibility, never grant it. PL-0303's approval rests on health.ts importing nothing and taking no rights, candidate or source, and on media-engine checking the rights allowlist FIRST and unconditionally. A shared floor module must therefore carry the threshold vocabulary ONLY -- no rights, entitlement, allowlist or candidate types, and no import of provider-sdk or media-engine -- so that the new module cannot become a route by which a health verdict reaches a rights decision. A test asserts the module's import graph is empty of those. NOT IN SCOPE: changing the value 0.5, changing the health algorithm, the prior/measured score split, the policy version enum, or anything PL-0303 delivered. PL-0303 is DONE and APPROVED at ad1e1ea4f3c9b95e10a6140aab7e8ecfdb597e77 and must not be reopened for this. If the correct home for the floor turns out to require a change inside PL-0303's delivered files, that is fine -- those files are on this task's surface -- but the health BEHAVIOUR proven by PL-0303's 31-mutant campaign must be unchanged, and the campaign's tests must stay green without being edited to accommodate the move.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck lint --force, exit 0, 22 of 22 tasks (11 typecheck + 11 lint), 0 cached. npx turbo run build --force, exit 0, 11 of 11. THE TYPECHECK MATTERS HERE BEYOND THE USUAL, because the delivered mechanism is that two packages now read ONE exported symbol rather than two literals that agreed: after this change a divergence between media-engine's PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR and provider-sdk's shipped failBelow is not a wrong value, it is a missing export, and tsc is what says so. The new leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/provider-health.ts resolves through the existing ./shared/* wildcard export, so no package.json, barrel or metadata edit was required and none was made.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks, 0 cached, 2667 passed 1 skipped (2652 passed 1 skipped before; +15, and the arithmetic is exact: contracts 202 to 208, provider-sdk 283 to 288, media-engine 369 to 373 -- 6 plus 5 plus 4). test:scripts 0 (38 environment, 69 control-plane, 16 validate-repo assertion groups, 35 dispatcher). repo:validate 0. NO PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGED AND THAT IS THE POINT, so no value-red against unmutated code was available and none was manufactured. The defect was that one threshold was written down twice -- media-engine's PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR = 0.5 and provider-sdk's failBelow: 0.5 -- with three doc comments and one runtime message ASSERTING they agreed, and no check that would go red on the commit that tuned one of them. Every existing test passed before and after, including ranking.test.ts's boundary pair at PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR - 0.01 and PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR exactly, which is precisely why prose was not enough. THREE MUTANTS WERE PLANTED AND ALL THREE WERE KILLED, each by the assertion written for it and by no other. M1, media-engine restates the constant: replacing `export { PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR }` with `export const PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR = 0.5` -- the exact pre-change state -- fails health-floor.test.ts 'declares no floor of its own' (1 failed, 3 passed). Note which assertion did NOT fire: 're-exports the same value under its historical name' stayed green, because 0.5 equals 0.5; a value-equality test alone would have permitted the duplication this task exists to remove, and that is why the source-graph assertion is the one carrying the guarantee. M2, the shared floor moves off the prior: 0.5 to 0.6 fails provider-sdk health-floor.test.ts 'keeps the prior sitting exactly on the floor' (1 failed, 4 passed), which pins the three-way coupling the value came from -- the Laplace 1/1 prior scores an unobserved provider exactly 0.5, the floor is 0.5, and the comparison is strict, so an unmeasured provider sits ON the floor and survives; any one of the three moving alone changes which providers are reachable at all. M3, the strict comparison becomes inclusive: `score < floor` to `score <= floor` fails contracts provider-health.test.ts twice (2 failed, 4 passed) AND media-engine health-floor.test.ts once, which is the cross-package half -- this is the mutant that would have buried every provider nobody has yet observed, permanently and silently, since a buried provider is never asked anything and so never accumulates the observations that would release it. THE ENTITLEMENT SEPARATION WAS WEAKENED IN ONE STATED WAY AND MECHANICALLY ENFORCED FOR THE FIRST TIME. PL-0303 was approved partly on health.ts importing NOTHING. It now imports exactly one module. That module imports nothing at all -- not zod, not a sibling -- and exports a number and a predicate over numbers; contracts provider-health.test.ts asserts the empty import list and the absence of any rights, entitlement, candidate, licence, allowlist or DRM vocabulary, and provider-sdk health-floor.test.ts asserts health.ts's import list is exactly that one specifier and nothing else. So the property is now 'imports one leaf whose transitive closure is empty', which is weaker to state than 'imports nothing' and, unlike it, is checked. Said plainly rather than left for the reviewer to notice. ONE HONESTY FIX CAME OUT OF THE WORK AND IS NOT COSMETIC: the fail-band reason trail asserted unconditionally that the policy's failBelow 'is also the floor below which the media engine excludes a candidate outright'. That is a claim about a different package and it is false for any versioned policy that moves its threshold -- it would tell whoever is reading the trail that a candidate is about to be excluded when media-engine would still serve it. It is now conditional on policy.failBelow === PROVIDER_HEALTH_FLOOR, and the third test in health-floor.test.ts drives both branches with a failBelow of 0.7. NOT DONE, and reported rather than quietly fixed: packages/contracts/src/shared/rights.ts still carries a stale note saying media-engine 'currently declares an equivalent PLAYABLE_RIGHTS' that should converge 'once PL-0201 is out of review'. That convergence already happened -- media-engine's PLAYABLE_RIGHTS is an alias -- so the comment is false today. It is inside this task's allowedPaths and it was left alone because it is a different duplication from the one this task was created for.

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests
